summary: Name the GDExtension library by the architecture of the host that builds it -- tools/build-native-bridge.sh from uname -m (aarch64 mapped to arm64) and tools/build-native-bridge.ps1 from the Windows processor architecture -- and repair every path that named the hard-coded x86_64 file: the macos arm64 rows in game/bin/project42_sim.gdextension, the macOS preset's universal binary_format and both architectures' dylibs in its include_filter, and the host-architecture assertions in verify.yml and nightly.yml. The end of it is E10's macOS job exporting and uploading a macOS artifact whose zip carries the dylib at the path Godot resolves.

coordination.notes: E10 recorded two blockers in game/ and refused to fake around them; this lane fixes them at their root, which is the build script's hard-coded x86_64 file name rather than the .gdextension alone. game/export_presets.cfg is touched on the macOS preset lines only (binary_format/architecture and include_filter); verify.yml on its library assertion step only. Nothing under godot-rust/src, game/scripts, content or docs/SHIP_PLAN.md. One path outside the card's Touches list: game/project.godot gains rendering/textures/vram_compression/import_etc2_astc=true, because Godot refuses a universal or arm64 macOS export while it is off and universal is the only macOS binary format the official template archive ships. No active claim held that file. It is one line under [rendering], additive, and changes no renderer behaviour.
